packs.name: 3I/ATLAS
packs.blurb: Only the third object ever seen passing through our Solar System from another star. The frame follows the comet, so it stays still while the background stars slide past.

packs.name: Synthetic test field
packs.blurb: Fake sky: a brown dwarf moves near the centre, a star to the upper left changes brightness.

packs.name: Barnard's Star
packs.blurb: The fastest-moving star in our sky: about 10 arcseconds per year, roughly 1.7 SPHEREx pixels between surveys six months apart.

packs.name: Epsilon Indi B
packs.blurb: Two brown dwarfs orbiting each other, together orbiting the star Epsilon Indi A. They move about 4.7 arcseconds per year.

packs.name: 10 Hygiea
packs.blurb: The fourth-largest asteroid in the main belt, about 430 km across. The frame follows it over several days.

packs.name: R Draconis
packs.blurb: A pulsating red giant whose brightness swings by a large factor over about 8 months. Compare its brightness between epochs.

packs.name: RW Aurigae
packs.blurb: A young star still surrounded by its planet-forming disk, which periodically dims it. Watch its brightness, not its position.

packs.name: WISE 0855-0714
packs.blurb: The coldest brown dwarf known (about -25 C), only 7.4 light years away. Very faint and very red: look at the longest-wavelength detector.
